text: The study says masks are unnecessary; according to experts, we can stop wearing them.
premises: The study says masks are unnecessary; experts say so.
reasoning_explanation: Authority invoked without clear identification of source or study quality.

text: It is raining, therefore the fields will be dry.
reasoning_explanation: Direct polarity conflict between premise and claim.

text: Traffic increased last year; therefore the new policy must have failed.
reasoning_explanation: Correlation cited without causal link; inference is weak.

text: Just as a lock keeps a door secure, encryption keeps data private; so we need stronger locks on our servers.
premises: Encryption is like a lock that keeps data private.
reasoning_explanation: Analogy present but mapping between physical locks and server operational measures is not established.

text: The medication worked on mice; therefore it will work on humans.
Because the product had five-star reviews, it's the best on the market.
reasoning_explanation: Appeal to reviews without considering sampling bias or review authenticity.

text: The sky is clear; therefore it must be snowing.
reasoning_explanation: Explicit contradiction between observation and claim.

text: Studies show a link between A and B; hence A causes B.
premises: Studies show a link between A and B.

text: Like how a map helps you find a city, this summary will replace the full report, so we don't need to read it.
claim: We don't need to read the full report.
premises: The summary is like a map that helps find a city.
reasoning_explanation: Analogy overgeneralizes tool utility to replace full evidence.

text: The thermometer shows 25°C; therefore the water is boiling.
reasoning_explanation: Premise contradicts claim (25°C is far below boiling).
